heading: Praggnanandhaa ends Anish Giri’s winning streak as India’s men outplay Netherlands at Chess Olympiad
author: Amit Karmarkar / TNN /  Sep 21, 2026, 09:03 IST
paragraphs: Anish Giri of The Netherlands showed his adventurous side but could not continue the offensive against R Praggnanandhaa

The Indian weathered the storm, refused a draw offer in an equal position after 34 moves and displayed his grit and unrelenting approach to eke out a win after five hours and 58 moves of Scotch opening.Though top seeds in both sections — USA in the open and Indian women — were shocked by Germany and Poland respectively, wins by Pragg and D Gukesh meant defending champions Indian men stole the limelight at Chess Olympiad in the fifth round in Samarkand on Sunday
They outplayed the Dutch 3-1 as Arjun Erigaisi and Nihal Sarin drew their games.R Vaishali could not pose enough threats to Aleksandra Maltsevskaya from a better position which eventually collapsed
K Humpy, Divya Deshmukh and Vantika Agrawal drew their games

India rested B Savitha Shri, who was on a four-game winning streak and played Vantika who drew with more celebrated Monika Socko.Though Vaishali and India went down to Poland for the second successive year, her brother Pragg gave India reason to smile with a pivotal win over Giri.Gukesh, who got up from his chair to take a glance at Pragg’s position on more than one occasion when Giri was calling the shots, scored a clinical win on the fourth board over Erwin L’Ami.It was India’s first win on the top board that ended Giri’s run of four successive wins in the tournament
They lead the table jointly with Uzbeks and Germany
Frederick Svane, who had ousted Gukesh in the last year’s World Cup in Goa, led fifth seed Germany’s 2.5-1.5 win over USA
